security_audit.summary: All 48 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, legitimate service links, placeholder syntax, credential storage documentation, or model routing. A separate concern is unsafe prompt substitution into shell examples despite a blanket claim that prompt content cannot cause shell injection. No evidence found of malicious intent; CLI privacy and security claims cannot be verified from this documentation-only package.

remediation.issue: Prompt placeholders occur inside single-quoted shell arguments, but the documentation claims there is no prompt injection surface through the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured JSON serialization and a subprocess argument array without a shell. Remove the blanket assurance and document safe handling of quotes.

semantic_findings.description: Examples place prompt placeholders inside single-quoted shell arguments, while line 182 states: "No shell injection surface from prompt content." Direct substitution of untrusted prompt text containing a single quote can escape the argument and execute shell syntax before the CLI receives JSON.

content.value_statement: Video requests require clear motion prompts and compatible model settings. This skill guides Wan 2.7 generation through RunComfy with optional audio-driven lip-sync.
actual_capabilities: Guide text-to-video requests through the RunComfy CLI using the Wan 2.7 endpoint.
Configure duration from 2 to 15 seconds, 720p or 1080p resolution, and five documented aspect ratios.
Add a WAV or MP3 audio URL for audio-driven lip-sync.
Control prompt expansion, negative prompts, and seeds for video variations.
Provide camera-motion guidance and sample product, spokesperson, and vertical-video prompts.
Explain CLI authentication, output-directory selection, and documented exit codes.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account, authentication, the separately installed CLI, and network access; the package contains documentation only.
Clips are limited to 15 seconds and 1080p, with five documented aspect ratios.
Audio must be WAV or MP3, 3 to 30 seconds, and no larger than 15 MB.
Multi-reference support is claimed, but the documented input schema provides no reference-media parameters.

best_practices: Specify camera motion and one primary action before adding lighting or style details.
Use approved media, check audio constraints, and avoid sending confidential content to the remote service.
Serialize JSON and pass CLI arguments without shell interpolation; disable expansion when exact prompt wording matters.
anti_patterns: Substituting untrusted prompt text directly into single-quoted shell examples.
Requesting native 4K, clips longer than 15 seconds, or unsupported audio formats.
Assuming multi-reference inputs work without checking the current provider schema.

faq.question: What must I install before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and authenticate with a RunComfy account. The skill itself supplies documentation, not the model or CLI.

faq.question: Which durations and resolutions are documented?
faq.answer: The documented duration range is 2 to 15 whole seconds. Resolution options are 720p and 1080p.

faq.question: Can I supply my own voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply an audio URL for a WAV or MP3 file lasting 3 to 30 seconds and no larger than 15 MB.

faq.question: Can I prevent automatic prompt rewriting?
faq.answer: Yes. Disable prompt expansion when preparing the request to preserve literal prompt wording.

faq.question: Does the documented schema support multiple reference files?
faq.answer: The text claims multi-reference support, but its schema lists no reference-media parameters. Check the current provider documentation before relying on that capability.

faq.question: Does generation run locally?
faq.answer: No. The local CLI submits model inputs to RunComfy and downloads generated results. Review provider privacy terms before sending sensitive material.
